title: Grant the PIM Manager engine identity its missing permissions
purpose: Give the PIM Manager engine identity the Microsoft Graph (and other API) application permissions and Azure role assignments it is missing.
whenToRun: When PIM Manager shows this command (Overview > permission check, or the Get Started step "Engine permissions"), with your environment's values filled in. PIM Manager itself never grants a permission: an identity that could, could give itself anything. Safe to run again: what the engine already holds is reported and left alone.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: Granting an application permission (an app role assignment) to a service principal needs a Privileged Role Administrator or a Global Administrator. Only needed for -GraphPermissions / -AppRoles.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: each scope in -AzureRoleAssignments (for the tenant root: the root management group); Owner works too
runAs.why: Creating an Azure role assignment needs User Access Administrator or Owner at that scope. At the tenant root a Global Administrator first turns on 'Access management for Azure resources' (Microsoft Entra ID > Properties). Only needed for -AzureRoleAssignments.

runAs.name: delegated Microsoft Graph scopes AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All and Application.Read.All
runAs.scope: the browser sign-in (first-party public client 'Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools')
runAs.why: What the browser sign-in asks for: read the engine identity and the API's permissions, and create the app role assignment. No PowerShell module, no certificate, no secret.

runAs.name: delegated Azure Resource Manager access (user_impersonation)
runAs.scope: the second browser sign-in (first-party public client 'Microsoft Azure PowerShell'), only for Azure roles
runAs.why: Reads role definitions and the engine's role assignments, and creates the missing assignment as you.

changes.object: application permission for the engine identity: an app role assignment (POST servicePrincipals/{API}/appRoleAssignedTo) for each name in -GraphPermissions (Microsoft Graph, e.g. Group.ReadWrite.All) and -AppRoles (another API, as <permission>@<API application id>)
changes.permission: each application permission you pass -- PIM Manager's command names exactly the ones its permission check found missing
changes.why: The engine applies the access you define in PIM Manager through these APIs; without the permission that part of the engine fails.
changes.undo: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the engine identity > Permissions > remove the permission (or DELETE servicePrincipals/{engine}/appRoleAssignments/{id}).

changes.object: Azure role assignment for the engine identity (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, principalType ServicePrincipal) for each '<role>@<scope>' in -AzureRoleAssignments
changes.permission: the Azure role you pass, by name or role definition id: Reader (what PIM Manager asks for at the tenant root, so discovery can see Azure), optionally User Access Administrator (only when the engine must assign the Azure resource roles you delegate); Owner, Contributor and Role Based Access Control Administrator are also recognised by name, any other name is looked up at the scope
changes.scope: the scope you pass: the tenant root management group, a management group, a subscription or a resource group
changes.why: Discovery reads Azure with Reader; assigning delegated Azure resource roles needs User Access Administrator. PIM Manager never asks for Owner or Contributor.
changes.undo: Azure portal > the scope > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments > remove the engine identity's assignment.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.default: the tenant you sign in to
parameters.help: Your tenant id; a sign-in that lands in another tenant is refused.

parameters.name: EngineObjectId
parameters.help: Object id of the engine identity's service principal (shown in PIM Manager).

parameters.name: GraphPermissions
parameters.help: Microsoft Graph application permissions to grant, e.g. 'Group.ReadWrite.All','RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory'.

parameters.name: AppRoles
parameters.help: Application permissions of other APIs as '<permission>@<API application id>'.

parameters.name: AzureRoleAssignments
parameters.help: Azure roles as '<role name or role definition id>@<scope>'.

parameters.name: UseEdge
parameters.help: $true opens Microsoft Edge for the sign-in; $false the default browser.

parameters.name: GraphAccessToken
parameters.help: Automation: a Microsoft Graph token (delegated AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All + Application.Read.All) instead of the browser sign-in.

parameters.name: ArmAccessToken
parameters.help: Automation: an Azure Resource Manager token instead of the second browser sign-in.

parameters.name: PlanOnly
parameters.help: Read and report what would be granted; change nothing (as -WhatIf).

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.help: Also return the result rows as objects.

readsOnly: the engine identity's service principal (name, type) and the application permissions it already holds
each API's service principal and the application permissions it offers (Microsoft Graph, or the API in -AppRoles)
Azure role definitions (by name) and the engine identity's role assignments at and above each scope
network: localhost (the browser returns the sign-in to a local port on this computer)
whatIf: Signs in and reads, prints the plan (already there / would grant / refused per permission), then one "What if:" line per grant: the application permission and the API, or the Azure role and its scope. Nothing is granted.
undo: Remove each app role assignment from the engine identity (Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the engine identity > Permissions) and each Azure role assignment (Access control (IAM) at the scope). The script creates nothing else.
